text: What if you dug a hole straight down and never stopped?
formula: title question, spoken word for word (STANDARD 1.3)

text: This tiny lemon tree needs a hole. Thirty centimetres deep.
formula: stake: a small potted tree needs a ~30 cm planting hole (the thread of the video)

text: Two metres. You hit the water pipe. That's on you.
formula: household water pipes are usually buried ~0.5-1.5 m deep, so a 2 m hole has passed one; temperature ~15 C (near-surface ground stays near the yearly average air temperature)

text: Sixty metres. Twenty storeys deep. Your neighbour films instead of helping.
formula: one storey ~3 m -> 60 m / 3 m = 20 storeys

text: Three hundred and fifty metres. The Eiffel Tower would fit inside.
formula: Eiffel Tower height 330 m (with antennas) < 350 m

text: Over two kilometres. Deeper than the deepest cave ever explored.
formula: Veryovkina Cave (Abkhazia, Georgia), deepest known cave: 2,209 m (Wikipedia; record 2,212 m reported 2018) < 2,300 m

text: Four kilometres. The world's deepest mine. The rock is over sixty degrees.
formula: Mponeng gold mine, South Africa: deepest mine from ground level, over 4 km; rock face up to ~66 C (Wikipedia / Wired 2011)

text: Twelve kilometres. Scientists took nineteen years to drill this deep.
formula: Kola Superdeep Borehole: drilling began 1970, reached 12,262 m in 1989 -> 1989 - 1970 = 19 years; ~180 C at depth (Wikipedia)

text: Thirty-five kilometres. You're through the crust. The tree needed thirty centimetres.
formula: Moho (crust-mantle boundary) under continents: 20-90 km, average 35 km (Wikipedia); ~500 C at the top of the mantle (EBSCO); 35,000 m / 0.3 m = 116,667x deeper than needed

text: A hundred kilometres. The rock glows. Your neighbour loves the lighting.
formula: base of the lithosphere ~100 km, ~1,300-1,400 C (LibreTexts Physical Geology table 9.2: 0-100 km -> 0-1400 C); rock visibly glows above ~525 C (Draper point)

text: Almost three thousand kilometres. The core. Liquid metal. About four thousand degrees.
formula: core-mantle boundary 2,890 km (EBSCO; Live Science ~2,900 km); temperature ~3,500-4,000 C (LibreTexts 3,800 C; EBSCO 4,000 C); outer core = liquid iron-nickel

text: The centre of the Earth. About as hot as the Sun's surface.
formula: mean Earth radius 6,371 km; core ~5,000-5,500 C 'about as hot as the surface of the sun' (Live Science); Sun's surface ~5,500 C (5,772 K)

text: Keep going, and you pop out in New Zealand.
formula: Earth's diameter = 2 x 6,371 = 12,742 km; the antipode of Madrid (40.42 N, 3.70 W) is 40.42 S, 176.30 E = near Weber, New Zealand (findlatitudeandlongitude.com antipode map)

text: And the tree? Still in its pot.
formula: punchline: pays off the stake from line n1

text: What should we try next? Tell us in the comments.
formula: ending ask over the last shot (STANDARD 1.8)
